merger_description:
ASSA ABLOY Holding AB, a holding company in the ASSA ABLOY Group (**ASSA ABLOY**), proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Gunnebo Entrance Control AB and its subsidiaries (**GEC**) (The **Acquisition**).

ASSA ABLOY is a provider of access solutions, including locking, access control systems and components, and entrance automation (e.g., automatic pedestrian doors and industrials doors). ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems (**AAES**) is a division of ASSA ABLOY which focuses on the manufacture and supply of entrance automation, operating globally under brands including ASSA ABLOY and agta record. ASSA ABLOY also distributes other products, which broadly encompasses physical security and storage solutions, access and locking solutions, doors and secure transfer solutions.

ASSA ABLOY and AAES are active in production and sales of security entrance control equipment, but do not provide after-sales services for these products.

In Australia, GEC is active in security entrance control equipment and services, supplying speed gates, turnstiles, mass transit gates, retail gates and security revolving doors which it manufactures at its four production sites located in Italy, Czechia, the USA and China. GEC offers after-sales services in relation to its own security entrance control equipment. GEC also distributes third-party products including safes, cabinets, vaults, manual doors and bollards.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, submissions from third parties and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The aggregation resulting from the Acquisition is estimated to
be low in the relevant markets for the supply of:
• Security control equipment.
• Speed gates.
• Security revolving doors.
• Access control systems.
• Post-Acquisition, the merged entity would continue to face
competition from multiple alternative suppliers in each of these
markets.
• For airport exit lanes, ASSA ABLOY would continue to face
competition from alternative solutions that serve the same
purpose and from multiple alternative suppliers of airport exit
lanes.
